land.text: Hubei, the Xin province where the Lülin bands rose

predecessors.note: The Lülin held ground the pages do not describe; Hubei is the only place the Xin page gives.

land.text: the Lülin lands, which become the Gengshi Emperor's restored Han

successors.note: Wang Mang page: 'in early 23, Liu Xuan was proclaimed the Gengshi Emperor'; the Xin page has 'Han restorationist armies' beating the Xin at Kunyang in June-July 23. The pages do not say in so many words that the Lülin army is the Gengshi army.

correction.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 17-22. No Cliopatria row. The Xin page gives only 'two insurgent bands in Hubei'; the outline is the province of Hubei, a proxy for the mountain bases and the Jingzhou lands that a gap-filler should find. Cliopatria's Xin shape loses 364 Hubei cells by 23 (xin-dynasty keyframe).

region.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

ledger.note: About 17: the Lülin bands rise in Hubei. 'two insurgent bands in Hubei were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page); 'About AD 17, as the burdens from the wars and the corruption continued to increase and famines occurred, several rebellions began' (Wang Mang page); the Xin page: 'large-scale civil war by 19 AD'. Reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19): source moved to the Wang Mang page, which gives the year ('About AD 17') and the place ('Lülin rebels in modern Yichang, Hubei'); the Xin page gives no year.

region.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

ledger.note: About 17: the Lülin contest Hubei with the Xin; a mirror of the xin-dynasty ledger. Reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19): source moved to the Wang Mang page, which gives the year ('About AD 17') and the place ('Lülin rebels in modern Yichang, Hubei'); the Xin page gives no year.

region.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

ledger.note: 23: Kunyang and Chang'an. The Xin armies were 'completely defeated by Han restorationist armies in the Battle of Kunyang in June-July 23 AD' and 'Chang'an captured: 5 October 23 AD'; the Lülin plague of 22 killed 'about half of the rebels' (Wang Mang page).

region.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

ledger.note: 23: the Lülin are absorbed by the Gengshi Emperor's restored Han. 'In early 23, Liu Xuan was proclaimed the Gengshi Emperor'; the Gengshi Emperor 'took the throne in 23 and was deposed by the Red Eyebrows' (Wang Mang page). Confidence 2: the pages do not name the Lülin as his army.

wars.name: Lülin and Chimei rebellions (fall of the Xin)

zones.text: Hubei, where 'two insurgent bands ... were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page)

wars.outcome: Rebellions from about 17 became a civil war by 19; the restorationist armies beat the Xin at Kunyang in June-July 23 and took Chang'an on 4-5 October.
wars.note: See the same war in xin-dynasty.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Lülin lands; Hubei is a province proxy.

sources.title: Xin dynasty
sources.note: Proclaimed 10 January 9; Chang'an captured 5 October 23; Xiongnu war 10/11; Kunyang 23; no area figure. Thin.

sources.title: Wang Mang
sources.note: Accession, Chang'an renamed Chang'an (constant peace), Xiongnu seal change, Western Regions troubles from 10 and 16, rebellions about 17, Gengshi Emperor early 23, Chang'an sacked 4 October, death 6 October 23.

notes: Written by ea-02-c as a rebel dossier because the Xin's fall (rule 5) needs a rebel counterpart that no Cliopatria row covers. Thin by necessity: the Xin and Wang Mang pages give 'two insurgent bands in Hubei', the date 'about 17', the plague of 22 and Kunyang; no page opened gives the Lülin's bases (the Lülin mountains), leaders, capital or boundaries, so the single keyframe is the province of Hubei. Wikipedia title and Wikidata are null because no Lülin article was opened. The Gengshi regime (23-25) is carried inside han-dynasty.
